recent_posts.topic_title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes
recent_posts.author: psawyerberlin
recent_posts.content_text:
Update and a request for native speakers (Chinese and Spanish)
CKB Service Runner is live on mainnet and testnet, and there’s now a short “join” page for node runners in five languages:
中文: csr-monitor.chainsolution.net/join/zh/
Español: csr-monitor.chainsolution.net/join/es/
English: csr-monitor.chainsolution.net/join/
Français : csr-monitor.chainsolution.net/join/fr/
Deutsch : csr-monitor.chainsolution.net/join/de/
I checked English, French and German myself, but not Chinese and Spanish. If you’re a native speaker and spot an awkward or wrong phrase, especially the technical terms (全节点, 服务运行时, 受托人联盟…), please reply here. Every correction helps.
For the record: this is a volunteer project. My motivation is the one that grew out of this thread: a truly decentralised runtime on CKB, where jobs that today need a bot on someone’s server, or a trusted federation, run on a ranked network of independent full nodes instead. As @Ayoub_Lesfer’s CrowdCell example showed, many apps need exactly that. I believe it can make CKB unique.
Thanks to everyone who shaped the idea here!
PSBerlin

recent_posts.topic_title: CellScript Roadmap: Expanding the Frontier of CKB-Native DeFi
recent_posts.author: psawyerberlin
recent_posts.content_text:
Congrats on landing Part 1, Arthur. One thing in the roadmap caught my eye as Part 2 starts: several features need someone to submit a transaction later. That covers escrowed orders settled against a pool, expiry under #72, the non-custodial subscriptions in #74, and the signed intents in #76. As you say, a wallet timeout isn’t an on-chain expiry, and today that “someone” is usually a project’s own bot.
That’s the gap I’m working on with CKB Service Runner (CSR). An app posts a paid job cell. Registered runners, staked through a referenced Nervos DAO deposit, run an on-chain RISC-V service that reads the chain through host calls and returns a tx skeleton. Triggers can be at block/epoch/time, every k blocks (fits subscriptions) or when a cell is spent. They’re proven through since, and the job lock pays the tip only to a registered runner.
It might be worth a CellScript helper that emits a CSR job next to an order or subscription cell. That would keep “who executes this” explicit in the SDK, the same way you’re keeping enforceability explicit.
Honest status: runtime and contracts are testnet-only, mainnet paid services stay off until a service gate (history + runner diversity) is met, and audit fixes are in progress. It’s trust-minimised, not trustless. Happy to try a testnet integration if it’s useful.
Thread: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes
Code: CKB Service Runner · GitHub
Web: https://csr-monitor.chainsolution.net

Appreciate the suggestion, but I probably don’t plan to integrate CSR into CellScript.
Keeper coordination and transaction submission belong at the application layer, and adding CSR-specific support would introduce unnecessary coupling and maintenance overhead, I would leave such integrations to independent adapters.

topics.title: Spark Program | TalkDID — Bind did:ckb to Nervos Talk

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | TalkDID — Bind did:ckb to Nervos Talk
recent_posts.author: PANAGOT
recent_posts.content_text:
Problem: Nervos Talk accounts are ordinary Discourse logins. did:ckb exists elsewhere (Metaforo/DAO, Vellum, bbs.fans), but there is no Discourse × did:ckb plugin — mods cannot see on-chain identity on Talk without screenshots.
Solution: Open-source Discourse plugin + Theme Component (MIT after funding). User connects CCC → signs a short nonce → plugin verifies → stores bind on UserCustomField → badge on profile/posts.
Non-goals: production Talk install (admin gate); DAO votes; Fiber tips; another DID tutorial.
Why Spark / CKB: Committee already redirected a prior DID ask toward Discourse + CKB DID. App-layer, Talk-native, OSS.
Ask: $500 (CKB equiv.)
M1 $250 (week 1): plugin scaffold, challenge/sign/verify, UserCustomField, tests, public repo + Docker Dev README
M2 $250 (week 2): badge UI, unlink/re-link, verify GIF + checklist, MIT, Spark update post
How to verify:
Live CCC testnet path demo: talkdid-ckb-j9kz.vercel.app
Example:
TalkDID verify
forum:talkdid-demo
user:talk-builder
network:testnet
nonce:a9ae84d1cc8327a59289690bcfa2052f
issued:2026-11-12T09:56:39.918Z
exp:2026-11-12T10:06:39.920Z
Currently forum doesn’t allow me to post any images and links.

recent_posts.author: Ksa_1971
recent_posts.content_text: What real problem does this project solve, and what practical value does it bring to users?
recent_posts.content_html: What real problem does this project solve, and what practical value does it bring to users?

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | TalkDID — Bind did:ckb to Nervos Talk
recent_posts.author: PANAGOT
recent_posts.content_text:
Good question, the real problem is trust on Nervos Talk itself.
Today a Talk account is just a normal Discourse login (email / password / Google). Someone can claim “I’m builder X / I’ve shipped Y / this wallet is mine,” but mods and readers cannot cryptographically check that on the forum. They rely on screenshots, Discord DMs, or “trust me.”
did:ckb already shows up in apps like bbs.fans and the CCF DAO Web5 stack, and tooling like Vellum can create/resolve DIDs but Nervos Talk itself is still a normal Discourse login with no on-profile bind, which is where Spark proposals and community debate actually happens
Practical value for users here
Proposers / builders | prove wallet / did:ckb control on your Talk profile and posts without leaving screenshots in every thread.
Mods / reviewers | See a verified badge next to the username when deciding whether an ask is from a real CKB identity, not a fresh sockpuppet.
Readers | “is this the same person as on Discord?” noise; identity travels with the post..

topics.title: Private payments in Cellula Wallet, on testnet

recent_posts.topic_title: Private payments in Cellula Wallet, on testnet
recent_posts.author: LusoCryptoLabs
recent_posts.content_text:
Private payments on CKB1600×900 50.8 KB
We have been building private payments into Cellula Wallet, and they now run on CKB testnet. This post covers what they hide, what they do not, what they cost and how we checked them. It describes what a user and the chain see, not the internals.
What stays private
On CKB every payment is public. Inputs name the cells they spend, locks show who held them, and capacity is the amount. A private payment in Cellula takes three things off that record:
Who paid. Nothing in the payment points to the payer’s cells or signature. It hides among the other payments in its group.
Who was paid. Each payment goes to a new one-time key, and only the receiver’s view key recognises it.
How much. Amounts are hidden, and the contract still checks that every payment balances.
These rules are enforced by a contract on chain, not by a server.
How it is used
CKB goes from your wallet into a hidden balance, moves privately inside it, and comes out to any address. There are two ways to be paid privately:
a private address, from one Cellula wallet to another;
a fresh ckt1 address that any CKB wallet can pay. The wallet then moves that payment into the hidden balance.
A view key lets someone else, an accountant for example, see what came in without being able to spend it.
Three moves, one shared hidden balance1600×900 67 KB
Groups of 16
A payment hides among the others in its group. A group holds 16 payments, and once it is full each of them can be spent.
Hidden among 161600×900 60 KB
The wallet draws the group as a circle of 16 places, so you can see the wait and the reason for it.
The waiting group in the wallet390×844 33.6 KB
If you do not want to wait, you can pay the empty places yourself. The payment is then ready at once, but it hides among fewer people.
Pay the empty places, or wait for free1600×900 74.1 KB
The wallet shows this before you confirm, along with what leaves your wallet, what comes back and what it costs.
Use it now in the wallet390×844 40 KB
Costs
There is a flat privacy fee of 12.25 CKB per note on testnet. It is the same for any amount, so it says nothing about the amount. A payment with change makes two notes. Each place holds 268 CKB while its group fills, and when the group closes 255.75 of it comes back to your hidden balance.
Measured and checked
The proof for a payment is made on the device that holds the keys. It takes about 25 ms in a desktop browser and 58 ms on an Android phone.
We sent 25 payments at the same moment on testnet. All of them went through, at about 9.5 a minute, and the slowest took under three minutes.
Every guard in the contract has a test that fails when that guard is switched off (56 of 56). An adversarial engine bent about 20,000 transactions against the contract and found nothing. On testnet, the node refused a note spent twice.
What still shows
What goes into the hidden balance and what comes out: the amount and the address.
That a payment happened, when, and which group it spent from.
A group filled mostly by one person hides them among few.
The node that receives a transaction sees an IP address.
So this is private, not anonymous, and it is only as private as the pool is busy.
What is hidden, and what still shows1600×900 62.1 KB
Try it
It runs on CKB testnet, in the Private tab of Cellula Wallet. Questions and reviews are welcome in this thread.

topics.title: Swap book: trade CKB for USDC, ETH or Bitcoin with no custodian (testnet)

recent_posts.topic_title: Swap book: trade CKB for USDC, ETH or Bitcoin with no custodian (testnet)
recent_posts.author: LusoCryptoLabs
recent_posts.content_text:
An update: the swap book’s code is now open.
GitHub - LusoCryptoLabs/ckb-htlc-swap: Atomic swaps between CKB and USDC, ETH or BTC: a hashlock lock on CKB, an order book and a market maker. Testnet. · GitHub (MIT licence)
What is in it:
the CKB lock that holds each side’s coins, with its tests and a build anyone can reproduce
the order book (server and page) and the market maker that keeps it stocked
the scripts that run a swap from end to end on testnet
We opened it so the builders here have more to work with. Take the lock, the book or the maker, and use whatever helps.
On security. This is a prototype running on testnet. Nothing in it guarantees the safety of funds. If you build on it, review every part that touches money yourself and test it against your own case. Our review notes are a starting point, never an audit.
Why a book and not another protocol. We think Nervos needs users before it needs more infrastructure. So we built something a person can open and use today, and now we are sharing the pieces under it.
Questions and pull requests are welcome.

topics.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC)

recent_posts.topic_title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC)
recent_posts.author: ebubedev
recent_posts.content_text:
Ask for Fiber eyes: coordinator fee on hold→payout without weakening escrow
Quick status: the live sell path is already the buyer-minted preimage design.
Buyer creates a payout invoice under H(S_b) on their node (Twine never sees S_b).
Hub new_invoice with payment_hash = H(S_b) and no payment_preimage → hold.
Seller pays that hold → status Received; inbound TLC stays held until RPC settle.
Hub send_payment on the buyer invoice (same hash) → learns preimage → settle_invoice / SettleReceivedHoldTlcSet.
Fiat never touches Twine. Cancel is refused once the hold is Received/Paid.
Today payout_invoice_ok forces buyer invoice amount == trade.shannons (hold amount). Fees are still 0%.
I want a per-successful-settle coordinator fee, ideally with incidence on both sides, without:
minting/storing S_b early,
a second lock that can strand the trade,
making the hub able to settle before the buyer is paid,
depending on fiat custody (fiat stays bank).
Why a fee at all: I need a sustainable way to keep a public Twine daemon/hub online — server, Fiber node liquidity ops, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance. Twine stays open-source and self-hostable; anyone can run a coordinator and set their own fee (including 0%). This is not a protocol rent on CKB. It’s operator upkeep for the node people choose to trade through.
Design I’m leaning toward
Treat the fee as the balance delta on the hub after a successful round-trip:
Hold invoice amount = H (what seller locks)
Buyer payout invoice amount = P where P < H (same payment_hash, different node, different amount)
On success: hub pays P, settles hold for H, keeps H - P in channel balance as the fee
For “both sides pay in CKB”:
H = principal + seller_fee
P = principal - buyer_fee
fee = H - P
Example: principal 100, 0.5% each → hold 100.5, buyer invoice 99.5, fee 1.0.
If the fee should leave the hub node, only after settle would I do a best-effort second send_payment under a new payment hash to an operator invoice. Trade settle must not depend on that hop.
Questions for people who know Fiber well
Amount asymmetry under one hash
Fiber treats payment_hash as unique per node, and hold fulfillment checks TLC amount against that node’s invoice (FinalIncorrectTlcAmount if underpaid).
Is it explicitly supported / safe for:
hub hold invoice = H
buyer invoice (other node) = P < H
same payment_hash / hash algorithm
then send_payment(P) → store preimage → settle_invoice on the hold of H?
Is the fee already “collected” as liquidity?
After settle, does the hub simply end +(H - P) (minus routing fees on the payout hop)?
If the operator is the hub, is a second fee payment unnecessary — i.e. is channel-balance accrual the idiomatic fee sink?
Ordering / auto-settle
Successful send_payment inserts the preimage locally and can trigger hold settlement. Any footgun if P != H (watchtower preimage registration, SettleReceivedHoldTlcSet, force-close claims)?
Over-lock (H > principal)
Any reason not to make the hold larger than the “trade principal” so the seller’s fee is real CKB, not only a fiat UI adjustment? Capacity / TLC / UX issues I should expect?
What to avoid
Which of these is a bad idea on Fiber?
separate seller fee invoice required before/with the hold
trying to bind fee + hold to the same payment_hash on the hub (I assume InvoiceAlreadyExists)
requiring the fee hop to succeed before marking the trade settled
any pattern that lets the hub settle the hold without a successful buyer payout
I care most about the fee path that stays compatible with hold-invoice escrow and does not compromise non-custodial guarantees.
Refs: twine, Fiber hold/settle_invoice behavior as in current fnn (we’re on the 0.9.1 line in deploy).
CC: @ArthurZhang @quake @RetricSu and others…

    • requiring the fee hop to succeed before marking the trade settled
    • any pattern that lets the hub settle the hold without a successful buyer payout

I care most about the fee path that stays compatible with hold-invoice escrow and does not compromise non-custodial guarantees.

Refs: twine, Fiber hold/settle_invoice behavior as in current fnn (we’re on the 0.9.1 line in deploy).

CC: @ArthurZhang @quake @RetricSu and others…

recent_posts.author: ArthurZhang
recent_posts.content_text:
I am in favor of introducing fees to make Twine financially sustainable. Running the hub, maintaining liquidity and handling disputes all come with real costs, and operators should have a viable incentive to keep the service running.
The proposed fee structure looks sound to me.
Two suggestions:
Please lock in the fee terms at trade creation, including the gross hold amount, net payout and rounding rules, so retries cannot change what either party agreed to.
Consider accounting for actual routing costs separately from the service fee, and ensure the hub has sufficient outbound liquidity.

Based on the Metaforo tally at close, the outcome is Passed. Approval is 100% against the required 51%, with total voting weight of 184,949,817 CKB against the minimum 15,339,253 CKB.
Post-close verification has been completed using CKB DAO Watchdog, together with a manual sanity check. Sixteen of the eighteen voters matched directly. The two flagged discrepancies were explained by withdrawals after the votes were cast: PSB withdrew 60,000 CKB after the last recorded vote in this poll, and Code3ks initiated withdrawal of 102,000 CKB after the poll closed. Both recorded weights were backed by DAO deposits when the votes were cast. These checks found no evidence of inflated or double-counted voting weight.
The FiberNuts proposal is confirmed as PASSED.
